html:
Byzantine emperor from 1391 to 1425, who ruled a shrunken state hemmed in by the Ottomans.

As a young man he was a hostage and vassal of the sultan, and had to march in Ottoman campaigns. When Bayezid I put Constantinople under blockade in 1394, Manuel went west to ask for help. From 1399 to 1402 he visited Venice, Paris and London, where Henry IV received him at Christmas 1400. Courts gave him honours but few soldiers.

The city was saved instead by Timur, who crushed Bayezid at the Battle of Ankara in 1402. In the Ottoman civil war that followed, Manuel won back some land and rebuilt the Hexamilion wall across the Isthmus of Corinth.

He was also a scholar who wrote letters, speeches and a dialogue with a Muslim scholar on faith. His sons John VIII and Constantine XI were the last two emperors.
sum: Byzantine emperor from 1391 to 1425, who ruled a shrunken state hemmed in by the Ottomans.
